target_customer: Providers of autism therapy such as applied behavior analysis, speech and occupational therapy clinics and schools
problem: Behavioral therapists take notes on paper and retype them into spreadsheets. Nightingale offered mobile data collection with customizable graphs and reporting.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for clinics and schools
product_category: Clinical data collection software for autism therapy

founders.name: Delian Asparouhov
founders.background_notes: YC and the 2014 TechCrunch and MedCity News articles name him as co-founder; the articles do not name other founders or give his background.

exit.reason: No shutdown notice found. A Wellfound page shows the app continued into at least 2016 and YC lists it as inactive.

competitors.name: Autism Tracker
competitors.what: Consumer app for collecting behavior data

technical_complexity.rationale: A customizable drag and drop data collection and graphing system on mobile with HIPAA compliant storage is moderate engineering for a team of two.

defensibility.rationale: Clinic data history could lock in customers, but pen and paper and generic spreadsheets were the real competition and reimbursement workflows needed integrations.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Catalyst (Lund founded it around 2010 per a vendor blog) and later CentralReach and others grew in ABA software. No acquisition of Nightingale was found.

market_need_then: MedCity News (2014-03-05) describes therapists taking handwritten notes and retyping them into Excel. Nightingale tested with five alpha schools from January 2014 (TechCrunch 2014-07-01). The long description cites CDC data of 1 in 68 children diagnosed.

branding.community_and_virality: Press from TechCrunch, MedCity News and Health Data Management. A later Nightingale 2.0 listing exists on Product Hunt. No community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Evocative caregiving name but shared with many products named Nightingale, and no evidence of brand driven growth.

pivots.why: Not stated; per search result summaries of a 2013 launch piece and later listings (not opened)

outcome_analysis: Nightingale built mobile data collection for autism therapists, tested with alpha schools in early 2014 and was raising seed money in March 2014. An aggregator reports a 660 thousand dollar seed in March 2015 and the app was still listed in 2016, but YC marks it inactive and no source gives a date or cause for stopping. The cause is therefore not public and failure factors stay empty.
notes: The 660K seed with a March 2015 date rests on one aggregator (StartupIntros); a second listing dates it 23.03.2015; investors are blank there. Parsers.vc lists Y Combinator and StartX, Wellfound lists Maverick Capital, Keith Rabois, Rough Draft Ventures and Thiel Fellowship among 13 investors without tying them to a round; these are not recorded. One search snippet says Asparouhov was a Thiel Fellow and MIT dropout, but the page was not opened so education is null. The medication reminder origin is from snippets only. The company website is not listed on YC and no fetch was possible, so the site is treated as unlisted.
